notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The digest above is from the last gate run, after the final reference generation; the report has no warning findings. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card lists helper PythonObjectDriver; this package is a direct decorated Driver over one of the card's two entry symbols, interface.module:Module. The other entry symbol, interface.controller:Controller, only exposes the FTDI setup and write_data/read_data; the piezo actuator with move/zero/set_closed_loop is Module. The driver declares one Module (one bay) per device; a multi-bay APT rack would be several devices or a future multi-resource driver, and APT.disconnect() is not wired because a Module has no reference to the APT object. The clone has no position or control-mode query: position and closed_loop are the last values the driver sent (0 and True at construction, from Module.__init__), not measurements, and their descriptions say so. Controller.read_data is only used by APT to poll the bay-used response and is not exposed. The PPS photodiode in pps.py is a separate VISA instrument and is not covered. No text file states the travel bound: max_travel is the constructor argument APT supplies, so position and move_piezo.position_um are Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json supplies an example 0..30 um window only, not a statement about a real stage. The hardware path (native.py) was never run; it requires pyftdi and the clone root importable, and this R1 package does not carry a reviewer sign-off. The fake is an in-memory stand-in that implements only Module.move, Module.zero, Module.set_closed_loop and the max_travel attribute; every number in it is marked as a placeholder.
